summary: Iteration 49 — validated all three shipped features: (1) Admin Ask Review Queue backend + UI, (2) Journal pinning/tagging backend + UI, (3) i18n key presence across sample locales. 14/14 backend pytest cases pass, all frontend flows work end-to-end. Original pending-review DB entry ('how do i prune tomatoes') left untouched — decision cycle tests use a seeded TEST_ key.
action_items: MINOR i18n leak: /app/frontend/src/i18n/locales/ka.js line 1006 has `"feedback.prompt": "Was this helpful?"` — untranslated English string in Georgian locale. All other 56 non-EN locales are properly translated for this key. Suggest translating to Georgian (e.g. 'ეს დაგეხმარათ?').

OPTIONAL enhancement: Journal.jsx has hardcoded English strings in the TagEditor (`Add plant tag`, `Edit tag`, `Save`, `Cancel`, `Tomato, roses, courgette…`) and on the paid page (`{n} pinned`, `Unpin entry`, `Pin to top`, `Unpin`). These bypass the i18n system. Not blocking (English is a valid fallback and 28-key sweep target keys are all present) but a follow-up sweep should add journal.pin/journal.unpin/journal.tag_add/journal.tag_edit/journal.tag_save/journal.tag_cancel/journal.tag_placeholder/journal.pinned_count keys.
critical_code_review_comments: ADMIN AUTH SHAPE INCONSISTENCY: /api/admin/ask/pending-review + /api/admin/ask/review/{key} accept `token` as a QUERY-STRING param (require_admin(token)). The frontend uses axios params: { token } so it lands in the URL. Sending an admin bearer via query string appears in access logs, browser history, and referrer headers — a mild secret-hygiene concern. Consider header-based (X-Admin-Token) auth or POST body across all admin endpoints going forward.

OWNERSHIP CHECK ORDER in POST /api/ask/journal/meta (routers/ask.py:465-476): the code first checks `ask_sessions` ownership, then checks the message belongs to that session — but does NOT verify the message's `role == 'user'` will actually match when it's the SAME user message id owned by another session. Not exploitable in practice (session-scoped ids), but the docstring says 'be a user turn' — the check enforces role='user' via the query, which is fine. Minor: return 403 rather than 404 when session belongs to another token, so callers can distinguish 'never existed' from 'not yours' — right now both are 404 which is standard practice, so this is a style nit.

AdminAskReview.jsx doesn't gracefully handle the case where a decide() call returns a network error mid-flight — the entry stays in the UI (not removed) but `busy` clears; user can retry, which is fine, but the toast surfaces the raw error message which could be a long stringified Axios error. Consider a friendlier fallback.

Journal.jsx pin/tag UI mutations are optimistic-only when the API succeeds — no local rollback if the POST /api/ask/journal/meta returns non-2xx. The updateMeta path (not shown here) should guard against a failed write so the visual pin state doesn't drift from the DB.

Test residue risk: the module-scoped seeded_session fixture creates ask_sessions/ask_messages/ask_journal_meta rows via pymongo but only cleans up at yield-teardown. If a test crashes hard between yield and teardown, TEST_ artefacts linger. Consider a session-level `autouse=True` autotouch fixture that wipes `{id: /^TEST_/}` at session start AND end.

All fixtures use sync pymongo (motor+asyncio.run causes 'Event loop is closed' across tests — do NOT switch back to motor here).
